summary: History of the Black Panther Party, founded in Oakland in 1966, and the FBI's COINTELPRO campaign under J. Edgar Hoover to discredit, divide, imprison and kill its leaders, including the 1969 police killing of Fred Hampton in Chicago.

evidence.note: Newton's 1942 birth in Louisiana and his childhood open the narrative
LBJ and Humphrey undermine the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party at the 1964 convention
Newton and Seale found the Black Panther Party for Self Defense in October 1966
Mulford Act gun-control bill aimed at Panther armed patrols, backed by Reagan and the NRA
segment on hostile mainstream press coverage of the Panthers
COINTELPRO refocused on the Panthers; forged documents and provocateurs described
1967 Oakland traffic stop shooting and Newton's trials
December 1969 Chicago police raid kills Hampton using informant's floor plan
1971 break-in at FBI office near Philadelphia exposes COINTELPRO files
1976 Senate committee report condemns COINTELPRO; latest period covered at length

notes: Title points at the FBI as the bastard, but half the story is Panther history, so both organizations are primary and roles are empty. J. Edgar Hoover is central but kept as a keyword to stay within five subjects. Newton's 1989 murder and the party's dissolution are brief mentions, so covered_span ends at the 1976 Senate report. California and Illinois are both central, so no single subdivision.
